strings.name: Jim Farley
strings.role: President and CEO of Ford Motor Company
strings.summary: Jim Farley is an American automotive executive who worked at Toyota and Lexus before joining Ford in 2007. He became president and CEO in 2020, pursuing changes in commercial vehicles, software services and electric vehicles. His career spans brand marketing, regional operations and group management.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Appointment announcements and effective dates, directors and CEOs, and honorary and earned degrees are distinguished; corporate transformation targets are not treated as completed results.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads changes in Ford's automotive business, advancing commercial vehicles, software services and electric products.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: A 1985 Georgetown economics graduate, he later earned a management degree from UCLA Anderson; Georgetown awarded him an honorary Doctorate of Humane Letters in 2026.
strings.facts.f2.label: Roles across companies
strings.facts.f2.value: Ford's president, CEO and director, he also joined the McDonald's board in 2026; the latter is not an executive management role.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Automotive business transformation
strings.highlights.h1.text: On taking office, he proposed expanding commercial-vehicle software services and electric vehicles while emphasizing quality, costs and execution; these were strategic directions at that time.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Marketing and regional operations
strings.highlights.h2.text: After Toyota and Lexus, he joined Ford and held leadership roles in global markets and Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Signs quarterly report certification
strings.timeline.t1.text: He signed the certification for the quarter ended September 30 as Ford's president and CEO.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Addresses alma mater's commencement
strings.timeline.t2.text: He discussed problem solving with Georgetown graduates and received an honorary Doctorate of Humane Letters, not a research doctorate.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joins McDonald's board
strings.timeline.t3.text: His director appointment took effect that day and was announced on February 10.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes Ford president and CEO
strings.timeline.t4.text: He succeeded Jim Hackett and joined the board; the appointment had been announced on August 4.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes Ford COO
strings.timeline.t5.text: He moved from leading New Businesses, Technology and Strategy to chief operating officer.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joins Ford
strings.timeline.t6.text: He moved from Toyota and Lexus to Ford, subsequently taking on marketing and regional operations responsibilities.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Toyota
strings.timeline.t7.text: He entered strategic planning and later worked in product and marketing roles in the United States and Europe.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduates from Georgetown
strings.timeline.t8.text: He majored in economics; an assertion of two bachelor's degrees not confirmed by the university is not adopted.
